claims.text: WTaTiVZr is an equimolar five-element alloy.
WTaTiVZr has improved high-temperature plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr has improved high-temperature toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Lattice-distortion-induced grain-boundary engineering is the primary cause of the proposed plastic-strain and toughness improvements.
Multi-element lattice distortion promotes a fine, equiaxed grain structure in WTaTiVZr.
Multi-element lattice distortion promotes a high dislocation density in WTaTiVZr.
The proposed grain-boundary structure enhances grain-boundary sliding during high-temperature deformation.
The proposed grain-boundary structure enhances dynamic recovery during high-temperature deformation.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recovery impede catastrophic crack propagation.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recovery permit more uniform plastic deformation.
The proposed WTaTiVZr starting material has a refined, near-equiaxed microstructure, whereas the pure-tungsten comparator is conventionally processed and recrystallized.
Ti- or Zr-derived intermetallic or oxide nanoprecipitates may stabilize the WTaTiVZr grain structure.
Pure tungsten has limited slip systems under the proposed conditions.
Pure tungsten is prone to early embrittlement or brittle behavior relevant to plasma-facing service.
WTaTiVZr will have a lower yield stress than pure tungsten at 1000–1200 °C.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit observable grain-boundary-mediated deformation features after high-temperature loading.
The proposed mechanism applies roughly from 1000 °C to 1200 °C.
The proposed mechanism applies only under loading regimes in which grain-boundary dynamics are active.
Outside the stated conditions, oxidation or phase transformations may dominate behavior.
Processing variability can alter grain refinement and precipitate populations and thereby change the relative contributions of dynamic recovery and solid-solution strengthening.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field specifies a refined WTaTiVZr microstructure versus conventionally processed recrystallized tungsten, while the falsification design proposes matched processing and comparable initial microstructures. The former intentionally confounds composition with microstructure, whereas the latter attempts to control that difference.
